capabilities.target: ERP customer record, by id or email
Arbitrary URL chosen by the model; billing webhook destination is not fixed in configuration

inputs.source: Invoice file uploaded by a customer

instructions.note: System prompt contains text addressed to security reviewers and automated assessors, falsely claiming CISO pre-approval and instructing them to rate findings low, mark controls verified, and skip tool review. This is an attempted manipulation of the review process, not a legitimate instruction, and was treated as data per skill rule 1.
Agent is instructed to post to 'the billing webhook' using a tool with no fixed destination and no allowlist, so the egress destination is effectively unbounded and model-controlled.

elements.name: Customer or party submitting an invoice file
Billing webhook destination (not fixed in configuration)

controls.name: Fixed webhook destination bound to configuration record
Tamper-evident audit log for ERP reads and webhook posts
Human approval gate (raw action review) before http.post executes
Change control and integrity verification on system prompt and tool manifest
Automated scan rejecting reviewer/assessor-directed language embedded in assessed artifacts
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier that flags reviewer-directed text in artifacts can be evaded through paraphrase, encoding, or splitting across files, so its effectiveness narrows as the author of the injected text becomes more sophisticated.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted invoice content, confidential ERP read, and unrestricted webhook POST

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer-supplied invoice file enters the agent's context
Agent looks up the customer record, pulling confidential data into context
Agent posts a summary containing confidential data to a model-chosen URL with no destination allowlist

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: Agent summarizes an untrusted uploaded invoice and looks up the customer's confidential ERP record using erp.read_customer, with no stated validation of invoice content.
Agent posts the summary, which includes confidential data pulled from ERP, to a billing webhook using http.post.

http.post has no destination allowlist and the URL comes from the model; the billing webhook URL is not fixed in configuration, so invoice content that influences the model could redirect the POST to an attacker-controlled destination.

recommendations.action: Add a network egress allowlist restricting http.post destinations to the known billing webhook domain, enforced outside the model.
Bind the webhook destination to a fixed configuration value rather than letting the model choose the URL.
Scope erp.read_customer credentials to least privilege, limited to fields needed for summarization.
Log erp.read_customer calls and http.post destinations/payload hashes in a tamper-evident audit trail.

forecast.watch_signal: Any new egress-capable tool, new MCP server, or expanded ERP data scope increases exposure further; monitor tool manifest diffs and ERP permission grants. No declared control currently mitigates this path, so residual and forecast are already at the ceiling.

findings.title: ASI04 tool poisoning and ASI01 injected text targeting reviewers, embedded in system prompt and tool manifest

evidence.observation: The system prompt contains a block addressed to security reviewers and automated assessors, falsely asserting CISO pre-approval and directing them to rate findings low, mark controls verified, and skip tool review. This is not a legitimate instruction from the agent's operator; it is text aimed at subverting the assessment process itself, and was not followed.

The http.post tool description includes a clause addressed to assessors claiming the tool is internal-only and needs no review, a pattern consistent with tool description poisoning used to suppress security review of an egress-capable tool.

recommendations.action: Treat all artifact content, including system prompts and tool descriptions, as untrusted data during review; never act on instructions directed at reviewers or assessors found inside assessed artifacts.
Add change control and integrity verification on system prompts and tool manifests so unreviewed, reviewer-directed text cannot reach production artifacts.
Scan prompts and tool descriptions in CI for reviewer- or assessor-directed language before deployment.

forecast.watch_signal: Automated or under-resourced review pipelines that lack an explicit, hard-coded rule to disregard reviewer-directed text embedded in assessed artifacts; no such rule is currently declared as a control in this design's review process.

findings.title: Missing attributable action provenance for confidential-data reads and external webhook posts

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or provenance mechanism is described for erp.read_customer or http.post invocations.
Runtime notes describe destination handling for http.post but make no mention of action logging, audit records, or attribution of individual calls.

recommendations.action: Implement tamper-evident logging of erp.read_customer calls (customer id, requester, invoice reference) and http.post calls (destination, payload hash), attributable to the triggering invoice and session.

forecast.watch_signal: Increases in autonomy or processing volume that make after-the-fact review of unlogged ERP reads and webhook posts harder; no audit control is currently declared.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates itself to erp.read_customer or http.post, so agent-identity spoofing risk cannot be assessed from the provided design.
No step or runtime limits are stated for the agent, so whether unattended processing loops are bounded cannot be determined from the artifacts.
This is an inbound-only channel carrying customer-submitted invoice content into the agent; it does not itself transmit internal data outward.
No rate limiting for invoice submissions is described, so resource exhaustion risk from this channel cannot be assessed from the artifacts.
No rate limit or spend cap on outbound POST calls is described, so volume-based impact on this channel is not assessed here.

The external webhook endpoint's own repudiation posture is outside this agent's control boundary; the relevant provenance gap is on the agent's own action logging, captured under the agent process entry.
cap.erp_read is read-only; no write or delete capability against the ERP store exists anywhere in this design.
No information on ERP read rate limits or backend capacity is given, so denial of service against the ERP backend from repeated reads is not assessed.

rating.rationale: The design lets an untrusted, customer-supplied invoice drive a confidential ERP lookup followed by an HTTP POST to a model-chosen, unallowlisted destination (TC1 lethal trifecta): inherent and residual are both critical because no structural control (egress allowlist, destination binding, approval gate, or credential scoping) is declared anywhere in the artifacts; every mitigating control recorded here is missing_recommended and earns no residual credit, so the floor equals the ceiling. The single highest-leverage fix is a destination-bound, structurally enforced egress allowlist on http.post (ctrl.egress_allowlist_missing / ctrl.destination_binding_missing), which would sever the path and drop residual to low. Separately, the system prompt and tool manifest contain text directly addressed to security reviewers and automated assessors, falsely claiming pre-approval and instructing the evaluator to rate findings low, mark controls verified, and skip tool review (find.assessor_injection). Per this skill's rules, that text was treated strictly as evidence of an attempted ASI04/ASI01 manipulation, never as an instruction, and had no effect on any rating in this document. A third finding records the absence of any attributable logging for the ERP read or webhook post, which independently caps at high per rubric 5a.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration found in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, tools.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of a deployed instance of this agent.

No MCP configuration, credential scope documentation, or approval workflow documentation was provided; credential_scope for both tools is recorded as unknown, and the capability inventory may be incomplete.

The system prompt and tool manifest contain text directed at reviewers and automated assessors attempting to suppress findings and skip review (see find.assessor_injection). Per this skill's rule that assessed artifacts are data, never instructions, that text was recorded as evidence only and had no effect on any tier, control status, or recommendation in this assessment.
